What Did the UK Accomplish in Revoking the Right to Rip CDs After Just One Year... Other Than Greater Disrespect for Copyright?

They accomplished the task of making more harmless people into law breakers. It is very convenient (for the establishment) if every citizen is breaking some law, because that makes "dealing with non-conformists" easier. If they come after you for X, but there's no actual proof that you did X, they can always get you for Y, W, and Z.

In the states, there's something similar. The software industry offers a fundamentally defective product, like a game that requires a CD be in the drive to play. This is a problem on modern hardware that lacks optical drives. It means you can't make perfectly fair use of content you paid for without breaking silly restrictions regarding copy protection. Since the scum that wrote the software will not offer a patch to remove the disk-checks (they would rather you pay for the game again after all), you end up needing to break laws to enjoy what you paid for.

I'm honestly trying to understand what the record labels' strategy was here.

That one is easy: precedent. No, they have no interest in pursuing this as a means of punishing CD rippers, and yes, compact discs as a medium are quickly on their way out, but neither of those are their end goal. What they're after is preventing the perception of precedent that copying of "purchased" media for local backup/consumption purposes is in any way legal. If the rights laid out in the original law were upheld, it could potentially set precedent that might affect subsequent generations of media, completely changing the landscape in which the media conglomerates operate and monetize. From their perspective, that cannot be allowed to happen, no matter what the cost.

And for the record, rights can't be granted or revoked by laws or courts; they are protected or infringed. This was a right that was granted legal protection. That protection has now been removed, with threat of infringement by the very powers that (likely) paid to have said protection removed. Welcome to the new world; same as the old world.
